title: Python Basics - 15-question sampler
description: A short, friendly sampler built from the PythonQuiz platform's Unit 1 basics bank. Read the code, make a prediction, and use the review cards to learn from misses.
source: PythonQuiz platform / Unit 1: Python Basics (seed database)

questions.code:
a = [1, 2, 3]
b = a
a[:] = [4, 5, 6]
print(a)
print(b)
print(a is b)
questions.explanation: b = a points to the same list. Slice assignment changes that list in place, so both names see the new contents.

questions.prompt: What is the correct way to create a variable in Python?
questions.explanation: Python binds a name with an assignment such as x = 5; a separate type declaration is not required.

questions.prompt: What data type is the value True?
questions.explanation: True and False are Boolean values. Python also treats bool as a distinct type even though it behaves like an integer in some operations.
The + operator joins the two strings, producing Hello Alice.

questions.prompt: How do you get the length of the string 'hello'?
questions.explanation: Python uses the built-in len function for strings and other sized collections.
String indexes start at zero, so text[0] is the first character: P.

questions.prompt: String indices in Python start at which number?
questions.explanation: The first item is at index 0. Negative indexes count backward from the end.
% returns the remainder after division. 10 divided by 3 leaves a remainder of 1.
** is exponentiation: 2 raised to the third power is 8.
x += 3 is shorthand for x = x + 3, so x becomes 8.
10 > 5 is true, so Python runs the if branch and prints Big.

questions.prompt: Variables in Python must be declared with a type before they are assigned.
questions.explanation: Python is dynamically typed. The value assigned to a name determines its current type.

questions.prompt: How do you create an empty list in Python?
questions.explanation: [] is the list literal for an empty list. list() creates one too, but [] is the direct literal form.
Index 2 is the third item because list indexing starts at zero.
int(x) converts the text "5" into the number 5, so y + 3 is 8.
